I am excited to share with you my most recent project — filteredq.com.

This summer, I wanted to explore what it takes to build a startup — so I decided to turn an idea into reality.

As a student and tutor, I found it hard to get well-organized, relevant questions for your syllabus. Most question banks are cluttered and don’t use AI to help with your experience. While studying, I saw that practicing weak topics boosted my grades — but there was no tool that solved this problem.

With the experience I’ve gained from my first year studying Computer Science, I was able to bring this idea to life and finally solve a problem I couldn’t fix back when I was in school.

Tools used in the project:
Typescript
Main language — most of the application is written in TypeScript
Used for: Components, API routes, utilities, hooks, types

Javascript
Used for: Configuration files and utility scripts

SQL
Used for database migrations and schema definitions

Frontend
Framework: Next.js 14.2.23 (React-based)
UI: React components
Routing: Next.js App Router

CSS/Styling
Framework: Tailwind CSS

Other Tools
Supabase for backend, database, and authentication
Stripe API for payment integration
OpenAI 4o API for generating AI-powered explanations

From the pre-beta launch just 2 months ago, the platform has already grown to 1,500 users.

This project has helped me build a full-stack website from scratch and strengthen my skills in TypeScript, backend design, and product development — experiences I’m excited to keep building on.

🚀 Going forward, I plan to expand the question database and continue developing new features to keep improving the site and helping more students with their revision.
